_meta.provenance_policy: Every value carries provenance: 'sourced' (citation attached; bureau/primary or corroborated carrier source) or 'verify' (value present but resting on a secondary source or unconfirmed pairing — the engine applies it and surfaces it in the VERIFY queue). Values that change by policy year are stored as 'vintages' resolved by POLICY EFFECTIVE DATE; a policy effective before the earliest known vintage resolves to none and routes to human review.
_meta.scope: Workers' compensation premium audit rules. GL audit rules land in v2.
_meta.changelog: 2.0.0: real officer/sole-prop tables for 10 states from Aug 25 2026 research (NYCIRB RC 2659, WCIRB regulatory filings, PCRB Quick Reference/Circular 1813, NJCRIB via PIA, WCRB misc values, FSIGA, TDI/Texas Mutual, ICW Group carrier chart for DE/IL/GA pending bureau-direct confirmation). CORRECTION: prior NY values ($1,700/$3,400 wk, $89,200 flat) were refuted by NYCIRB RC 2659 and replaced.

officer_weekly_max.note: State-specific annual table — load per state

sole_prop_annual_basis.note: State-specific: flat basis, officer band, or no coverage election — load per state

audit_deadline_days.note: No general NCCI deadline; state-specific where set

anc_max_multiplier.source: ANC up to 2x estimated annual premium

uninsured_sub_full_charge.source: NCCI Basic Manual Rule 2-H-2: full subcontract price as payroll absent evidence of coverage, payroll records, or a definite payroll

uninsured_sub_materials_fraction.source: NCCI Basic Manual Rule 2-H-2 Subcontractor Table 2 (verified via NCRB's NCCI-based manual, https://www.ncrb.org/digitallibrary/basicmanual/Rule_2_-_Premium_and_Payroll.htm): labor+material contracts — not less than 50% of subcontract price when records don't segregate actual labor
uninsured_sub_materials_fraction.note: Full Table 2: mobile equipment with operators 33.33%, labor+material 50%, labor only 90%, piecework 100%. If verifiable records segregate actual labor, actual amount is used. Engine currently models the labor+material row; full table lands with contract-type intake.

monopolistic.source: Only OH/WA/WY/ND are monopolistic state funds

officer_weekly_max.source: NYCIRB R.C. 2659 — non-construction; construction employments capped separately at $1,922.25/wk eff 7/1/2026 (payroll limitation law, July 1 cycle)
officer_weekly_max.note: Two cycles in one state: Oct 1 rate revision + Jul 1 construction limitation. CORRECTED 8/25/2026: prior $1,700/$3,400 values refuted by primary source.

sole_prop_uses_officer_band.source: NYCIRB R.C. 2659: sole proprietors/partners (non-construction) use the same weekly min/max band as officers — no flat annual basis exists

uninsured_sub_materials_fraction.source: NY Manual Rule VIII.C.3.b (NYCIRB Digital Library, print 8/25/2026): absent the sub's payroll records — 33.33% mobile equipment w/ operators, 50% labor+material, 90% labor only; definite payroll from investigation controls if shown
uninsured_sub_materials_fraction.note: Uninsured construction subs also remain subject to NY payroll limitation and territory differentials (Rule VIII.C.3.c) — not yet modeled

audit_required_at_premium.source: NYCIRB Manual Rule VI: annual audit required at >=$5,000 premium

physical_audit_rule.source: NYCIRB Rule VI; RC 2516 permits remote completion of the records examination

audit_deadline_days.source: NY DFS OGC 03-04-12: audits within 180 days of policy expiration

class_system.source: WCIRB USRP — California classification system differs materially from NCCI

sole_prop_uses_officer_band.source: WCIRB: same annual min/max applies to partners, individual employers, and working LLC members

physical_audit_annual_at.source: USRP Part 3 Sec VI Rule 4, verified verbatim in the filed USRP eff 9/1/2026 (https://www.wcirb.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/2026-09_usrp-final.pdf): $10,500+ final premium -> physical audit at least annually; below -> physical at sufficient intervals + voluntary audit; dual-wage construction classes physically audited regardless
physical_audit_annual_at.note: History: $10,000 pre-2015; $13,000 eff 1/1/2015; $10,500 for policies incepting on/after 1/1/2020 (approved Sep 2019), unchanged through 9/1/2026 edition

uninsured_sub_materials_fraction.note: CA has NO WCIRB percentage rule: uninsured/unlicensed contractors are statutory employees (Labor Code 2750.5) and ACTUAL remuneration is the basis; materials deduction from contract price is carrier practice, not a bureau rule — route to reviewer

test_audit_program.note: Worksheets must be re-performable by a WCIRB examiner; insurers fined for vendor error patterns

bureau.source: NCCI state; FL DFS approves rate filings

officer_annual_min.source: FSIGA Executive Officer Payroll Limitation flyer (NCCI filing approved by FL DFS), https://fsiga.org/download/forms_and_documents/Flyer-ExecutiveOfficerLimitation.pdf
officer_annual_min.note: Construction officers: statutory half-minimum $33,800 — construction split not yet modeled

officer_annual_max.source: FSIGA flyer: $3,900/wk eff 1/1/2026 ($3,800 in 2025). Beware stale agency blogs citing $156,000 — refuted.
officer_annual_max.note: 2025 vintage ($3,800/wk) known but 2025 minimum unconfirmed; add both when confirmed

sole_prop_annual_basis.note: Electing sole props/partners flat basis — ICW Group carrier chart (3/11/2026) only; NCCI misc values paywalled. Confirm bureau-direct.

uninsured_sub_precharge_note.value: FL (NCCI Item 04-FL-2022, eff 3/1/2023): before charging additional premium for an uninsured sub, the carrier must verify the sub actually has non-exempt employees (for PEO-client subs, obtain the leased-employee list) and file notice with the FL Division of Workers' Compensation
uninsured_sub_precharge_note.source: https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2023/02/01/705477.htm; NCCI Item 04-FL-2022 (filing table percentages paywalled — UNCONFIRMED)

bureau.source: Texas Basic Manual is TDI-regulated; NCCI is statistical agent only. https://www.tdi.texas.gov/wc/regulation/

officer_annual_min.source: TDI Texas Basic Manual — static for many years
officer_annual_min.note: Static values; verify only if TDI amends the manual

officer_annual_max.source: TDI Texas Basic Manual — static for many years

sole_prop_annual_basis.source: SAWW x 1.25 x 52, resets each Oct 1; Texas Mutual DWC updates: https://www.texasmutual.com/blog/posts/2025/10/dwc-update-2026-average-weekly-wage

ot_premium_excludable.source: PA does not permit the overtime premium-pay exclusion

officer_weekly_max.source: PCRB Quick Reference; Circular 1813 (Filing No. 344) raised the max multiplier 2.5x->4x SAWW for policies eff 4/1/2025+ — a step-change: pre-4/1/2025 policies had a $3,200/wk cap
officer_weekly_max.note: Do not smooth over the 2025 step-change when adding older vintages

sole_prop_annual_basis.note: Individuals/partners not on payroll: min $70,044/yr, capped at officer max (ICW chart) — band-with-own-floor shape not yet modeled; route to review

ot_premium_excludable.source: DE does not permit the overtime premium-pay exclusion

officer_annual_min.note: ICW Group carrier chart (3/11/2026); confirm against DCRB Quick Reference Excel, https://dcrb.com/rating-values-list/

sole_prop_uses_officer_band.note: Individuals/partners not on payroll: min $72,072 / max $288,600 per ICW chart — same band as officers; confirm DCRB-direct

ot_premium_excludable.source: NJ Manual Part 3 Sec 3 Rule 35 (Remuneration Excluded), verified verbatim via NJCRIB Manual Amendment Bulletin #504, https://www.njcrib.com/Search/ViewPDF?id=1255 — the exhaustive exclusion list does not include overtime; full OT wage stays in the premium basis
ot_premium_excludable.note: CONFIRMED 8/25/2026 (was verify). Do not confuse with NJCCPAP, which strips OT premium only for the construction-credit wage calculation. Secondary charts (ICW) omitting NJ are unreliable on this point.

audit_adjustment_note.value: WI Basic Manual Rule V-C-3: carrier shall transact the premium audit adjustment within 90 days UPON ESTABLISHMENT OF ACTUAL PAYROLLS — trigger is payroll establishment, not policy expiration, so this is not wired to the expiration-based deadline check. Assigned-risk pool: audit within 90 calendar days after end of policy term.

officer_annual_min.note: ICW carrier chart ($1,450/wk); NCCI misc values paywalled — confirm bureau-direct

audit_deadline_days.source: 20 CSR 500-6.500(2)(A), https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/missouri/20-CSR-500-6-500: audits completed, billed, and premiums returned within 120 days of expiration/cancellation
audit_deadline_days.note: Exceptions: policyholder's documented failure to respond, or written agreement providing longer

bureau.source: NCCI state (LWCC is the state fund competitor)

audit_billing_notice_note.value: La. R.S. 23:1172.3 (amended eff 7/1/2025): insurer may not collect audit-generated premium without written notice within 90 days of COMPLETING the audit, and may not modify/complete a payroll premium audit more than 3 years after policy period end (exceptions: misrepresentation, noncompliance, disputes, fraud, court-ordered reclassification). Triggers differ from expiration-based deadline — modeled as compliance note, not wired to the deadline check.
